clue.text: Both shout wickedly about rookie's first sort of moustache

indicators.note: the shuffled letters go round, or about, the rookie's initial
doing something wickedly suggests mischief, so these letters are thrown out of their order
the first of rookie's letters is wanted, its initial

explanation.surface: Someone yells at a new recruit about the type of facial hair he is growing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wickedly' yields TOOTHBUSH from the shout's letters, and 'about' wraps that round the rookie's initial. The moustache is the small clipped square kind.
explanation.definitionFit: A toothbrush moustache is the small clipped square of hair under the nose, named for its bristly shape.

clue.text: Attempt to secure one pound for felt hat

indicators.note: the attempt word holds the other letters, securing them inside it

parts.note: a try is an attempt
I is the Roman numeral one
lb is the abbreviation for a pound in weight

explanation.surface: Someone tries to get a pound coin to buy a hat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to secure' signals the attempt word holding the rest inside it; 'felt' looks like a verb but is the hat's material.
explanation.definitionFit: A trilby is a soft narrow-brimmed hat made of felt.

clue.text: Working with Charlie, everyone standing by

parts.note: a machine that is working is on
Charlie is C in the NATO phonetic alphabet
all means everyone

explanation.surface: A colleague named Charlie joins everyone waiting on standby at work.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on call means available to be summoned at short notice, ready and waiting.

clue.text: One who idolises what Leander was?

definitions.meaning: in Greek legend Leander loved the priestess Hero, swimming the Hellespont nightly to her, so he worshipped Hero

explanation.surface: A question about the mythical lover's character.
explanation.walkthrough: Leander swam the Hellespont each night to see Hero; the question mark flags the pun on her name.
explanation.definitionFit: A hero-worshipper is a fan who admires someone excessively, idolising them.

clue.text: Talk about the old days, about short skirts, clubs, and start of experimentation

parts.note: re means about, concerning
minis are miniskirts
C is the abbreviation for clubs in card games

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Recalling the sixties: miniskirts, nightclubs and the first trying of new things.
explanation.definitionFit: To reminisce is to recall and chat fondly about past experiences.

clue.text: Conflict in group over head relinquishing power

indicators.note: in a down entry the group word sits over the rest

parts.note: a set is a group

indicators.note: relinquishing means giving up, so the power letter is dropped from the head word

parts.note: the top is the head of something
P is the physics abbreviation for power

explanation.surface: A boardroom clash in which the boss steps down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'relinquishing' drops P from TOP to leave TO; 'over' puts SET above it in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A set-to is a brief fight or argument, a conflict.

clue.text: Some seafarers, a long way away

indicators.note: only some of the letters of seafarers are taken, a run sitting inside the word

explanation.surface: A remark that certain sailors are travelling far from home.
explanation.definitionFit: Afar is an adverb meaning at a great distance, exactly a long way away.

clue.text: Something pink on flag I'm waving

indicators.note: a waving flag shifts about, so these letters are moved around

explanation.surface: Someone describes a pink design on the banner they're waving.
explanation.definitionFit: A flamingo is a wading bird famous for its pink plumage, so an example of a pink thing.

clue.text: Flag examined, we're told, then put out

indicators.note: we're told signals a word heard rather than seen, so the sound is what counts

parts.note: to have read a text is to have examined it
put out means annoyed, cross

explanation.surface: A banner was inspected, then set out on display.
explanation.walkthrough: 'we're told' turns READ (past tense, pronounced red) into its sound-alike RED.
explanation.definitionFit: The Red Cross is a flag, a red cross on white, used as the emblem of the humanitarian movement.

clue.text: Soul singer's heart broken by a candid and short note

definitions.note: the 's stands for is, joining the definition to the wordplay

indicators.note: a broken thing is in pieces, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: frank means candid

indicators.note: short means cut, so the note word loses its last letter

parts.note: a line is a short note or letter, as in drop me a line

explanation.surface: A singer's heart is broken by an honest, brief message.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broken' rearranges HEART to ARETH; 'short' cuts LINE to LIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Aretha Franklin was the American singer crowned the Queen of Soul.

clue.text: Suffer at home with scoundrel

parts.note: someone at home is in
a cur is a contemptible man, a scoundrel

explanation.surface: Someone endures life indoors with a rogue for company.
explanation.definitionFit: To incur a loss or penalty is to suffer it, have it fall upon you.

clue.text: Traffic warden needs me to help after call

indicators.note: the help word comes after the call word in the answer

parts.note: taken as written
to term something is to call or name it
aid means help

explanation.surface: A parking attendant says they need someone to assist them once they've rung.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' places the help word behind the call word; 'call' here means name, not phone.
explanation.definitionFit: Meter maid is a chiefly American, informal name for a traffic warden who checks parking meters.

clue.text: Obvious victory for former PM

parts.note: a bald statement is plain and obvious
a win is a victory

explanation.surface: A clear-cut election triumph for an ex-prime minister.
explanation.walkthrough: Stanley Baldwin was a British Conservative prime minister three times between the wars.
explanation.definitionFit: Stanley Baldwin led the UK government in the 1920s and 1930s, so he is a past premier.

clue.text: Expose and rile eccentric office worker with a long commute?

definitions.text: office worker with a long commute?

parts.note: to out someone is to expose them

indicators.note: eccentric means odd or off-centre, so the letters of rile are set out oddly

explanation.surface: Uncover and annoy a quirky colleague who travels far to work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eccentric' rearranges the second word's letters to LIER. The question mark flags a playful definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An outlier lives outside the area where they work, so their journey to the office is lengthy.

clue.text: Urge wards to bring a prosecution

parts.note: to press someone is to urge them
charges are people in one's care, wards

explanation.surface: Encouraging children in care to take someone to court.
explanation.definitionFit: To press charges is the idiom for formally accusing someone so a criminal case proceeds.

clue.text: Flabbergasted at cagoule in mail-order book

indicators.note: flabbergasted means thrown into confusion, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone is astonished at the price of a rain jacket in a shopping brochure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flabbergasted' rearranges AT CAGOULE. A cagoule is a lightweight hooded waterproof jacket.
explanation.definitionFit: A catalogue is a printed list of goods from which customers order by post.

clue.text: Model intoxicated, so stay put

parts.note: to sit for an artist is to model
tight is informal for drunk

explanation.surface: A drunk fashion model is told not to move.
explanation.definitionFit: To sit tight is the idiom for remaining where you are and waiting.

clue.text: Member of the clergy I located in large church

indicators.note: located in means placed within, so the I goes inside the church word

parts.note: a minster is a large or important church

explanation.surface: A cleric reports finding someone inside a cathedral.
explanation.definitionFit: A minister is an ordained clergyman, especially in Protestant churches.

clue.text: Their sisters trained dogs

indicators.note: trained letters are drilled into a new order, so these are rearranged

explanation.surface: Some siblings have taught their pets obedience.
explanation.definitionFit: Irish setters are a breed of red-coated gundog, so they are examples of dogs.

clue.text: Serious crime: leader denied motive

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter, and it is refused, removed

parts.note: treason, betraying one's country, is a grave crime

explanation.surface: A detective's frustration that a grave offence has no apparent motive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leader denied' removes the first letter T of TREASON.
explanation.definitionFit: A reason for doing something is its motive or cause.

clue.text: One after the other forming a line

definitions.meaning: objects ... are arranged in a line

explanation.surface: People queueing up in single file.
explanation.definitionFit: In a row means both consecutively and literally arranged in a straight line.

clue.text: Tourist runs into truck

indicators.note: the runs letter goes into the truck word

parts.note: a tipper is a truck that tips its load
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A sightseer hurries and collides with a lorry.
explanation.definitionFit: A tripper is someone on a pleasure outing, especially a day trip, so a tourist.

clue.text: Inflate article during ascent

indicators.note: during means within, so the article sits inside the ascent word

parts.note: a rise is an ascent
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Pumping up a balloon while it climbs.
explanation.definitionFit: To raise prices or a figure is to inflate it, push it higher.

clue.text: Light tail of razorbill, an aquatic bird

indicators.note: the tail of a word is its last letter

parts.note: taken as written
a tern is a seabird

explanation.surface: A birdwatcher notes the rear of one seabird and the look of another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tail of' takes the final L of razorbill.
explanation.definitionFit: A lantern is a portable lamp, so it is a light.

clue.text: Crowd harvesting

explanation.surface: A throng of people bringing in the harvest.
explanation.definitionFit: Gathering names both an assembly of people and the act of collecting crops in.

clue.text: One failing to win in close race

indicators.note: the answer sits in the words close race, spanning them

explanation.surface: Describing the runner-up in a tight contest.
explanation.definitionFit: A loser is anyone who is beaten, who does not come first.

clue.text: Go for a spin

definitions.meaning: your go in a game is your ...

explanation.surface: An invitation to take a drive.
explanation.definitionFit: Turn means both a go in a sequence of players and a rotation or short outing.

clue.text: Unusually, we're on hand at this time

indicators.note: letters arranged unusually are in a different order from normal

explanation.surface: For once, we are available to help right now.
explanation.definitionFit: The here and now is the present moment, so the phrase means at present.
